'''Ronald Ernest Grigg''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sridharan |first1=Visuvanathar |last2=Stevenson |first2=Paul J. |last3=Gunaratne |first3=H. Q. Nimal |last4=de Silva |first4=A. Prasanna |date=2023 |title=Ronald Ernest Grigg. 1 September 1935—10 January 2021 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=73|pages=175–197 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2022.0052 |s2cid=257639745 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (1 September 1935 - 10 January 2021) was a British [[chemist]] and [[Professor]] of [[Organic Chemistry]] at the [[University of Leeds]].<ref>[http://www.chem.leeds.ac.uk/People/Grigg.html University of Leeds staff page for Ron Grigg]</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sridharan |first1=Visuvanathar |last2=Stevenson |first2=Paul J. |last3=Nimal Gunaratne |first3=H. Q. |last4=Prasanna de Silva |first4=A. |date=2023-03-22 |title=Ronald Ernest Grigg. 1 September 1935—10 January 2021 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=75 |language=en |pages=175–197 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2022.0052 |s2cid=257639745 |issn=0080-4606|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Grigg was born in [[Southall]], to Ernest Ronald Grigg (a parcels packer) and Gladys Vera McBride (née Price).

Prior to university, Grigg worked at [[GlaxoSmithKline|Glaxo Laboratories]] from 1952 to 1960 whilst studying part-time for his first degree.  He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[University of Nottingham]] and undertook postdoctoral research at the [[University of Cambridge]] with the team led by Nobel Laureate [[Alexander R. Todd, Baron Todd|Alexander (later Lord) Todd]].

==Academic career==
Grigg was appointed to a lectureship in organic chemistry at Nottingham in 1965 and remained there until 1974 when he became Professor of Organic Chemistry at [[Queen's University, Belfast]].<ref>[http://reporter.leeds.ac.uk/474/grigg.htm ''University of Leeds Reporter'']</ref>  He was appointed Professor of Organic Chemistry at the University of Leeds in 1989.  He retired from Leeds in 2001 when he was made [[Emeritus|Emeritus Professor]].<ref>[http://www.leeds.ac.uk/secretariat/obituaries/2021/grigg_ron.html University of Leeds, obituary]</ref>

==Honours==
Grigg was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 1999.<ref>[https://royalsociety.org/people/ronald-grigg-11545/ Royal Society, profile of Ron Grigg]</ref>

==Private life==
Grigg married Jean Mary Rose Palmer in [[Ealing]] in 1956. They had two children: Stephen Paul in 1962, and Nicola Jayne in 1967.

Jean died in 2005. Ron Grigg died in Leeds on 10 January 2021.
